text: J.D. Power reported smart TVs with streaming capabilities were available in 74% of surveyed branded hotel guest rooms in its 2026 North America study.
limitations: Survey covers branded hotels in North America, not every hotel room.
excerpt: Availability increasing to 74% and guest usage rising to 62%.
locator: Key findings, ‘Today’s extras are tomorrow’s expectations’

text: J.D. Power reported 62% guest usage of smart TVs with streaming capabilities in its 2026 North America study.
limitations: Usage is among respondents in the branded-hotel study and does not establish satisfaction impact.
excerpt: Availability increasing to 74% and guest usage rising to 62%.
locator: Key findings, ‘Today’s extras are tomorrow’s expectations’

text: The 2026 J.D. Power hotel guest satisfaction study was based on responses from 44,787 branded hotel guests.
period: past 30-day stays between May 2025 and May 2026
limitations: Respondents were branded hotel guests.
excerpt: Based on responses from 44,787 branded hotel guests.

text: In 2025, J.D. Power reported that 40% of guests called smart TV or streaming capability a need-to-have amenity, compared with 21% in 2019.
limitations: The 2025 study was redesigned; historical comparisons should be treated cautiously.
excerpt: 40% of guests say smart TV or streaming is a ‘need to have.’

text: J.D. Power reported a 217-point satisfaction gap in 2025 between guests who experienced a hotel problem and those who did not.
limitations: This is hotel-problem evidence generally, not a causal estimate for display or casting failures.
excerpt: Guests who encounter a problem have substantially lower satisfaction.

text: AHLA projects U.S. hotel guest spending will reach nearly $805 billion in 2026.
limitations: Industry context only; no portion is attributable to connected screens.
excerpt: Hotel guest spending in 2026 is expected to reach nearly $805 billion.

text: AHLA reported rising operating expenses as a primary factor keeping 2026 GOPPAR at roughly 90% of 2019 levels.
metric: gross operating profit per available room versus 2019
limitations: Industry aggregate; individual property economics vary.
excerpt: GOPPAR at roughly 90% of 2019 levels.

text: ENERGY STAR lodging guidance says energy represents about 6% of lodging operating costs.
metric: energy share of lodging operating costs
limitations: Current guidance cites benchmark context that may predate 2026; it is not a new 2026 measurement.
excerpt: Lodging businesses spend approximately 6% of operating costs on energy.

text: ENERGY STAR lodging guidance says heating and cooling account for almost 40% of hotel electricity use.
metric: heating and cooling share of electricity use
limitations: Current guidance, not a newly measured 2026 industry average.
excerpt: Heating and cooling represent almost 40% of electricity use.

text: WTTC estimates Travel and Tourism contributed $11.6 trillion to global GDP in 2025.
limitations: Macroeconomic context only; not attributable revenue for connected hospitality screens.
excerpt: Travel and Tourism contributed $11.6 trillion to global GDP in 2025.

text: Current Samsung and LG hospitality offerings both describe guest-device casting or AirPlay capabilities for hotel-room televisions.
limitations: Availability depends on model, region, software, property network, gateway, and PMS configuration.
excerpt: Hospitality TVs support guest-device casting through vendor-specific deployments.

text: Samsung states that supported hotel TVs allow QR-based Google Cast or Apple AirPlay pairing without a separate login and automatically delete connection information at checkout.
limitations: Vendor-stated; model, device, software, and regional availability vary.
Secure deployment still depends on property network and integration design.
excerpt: No separate login is required, and device connection information is automatically deleted upon checkout.
locator: Frame hospitality announcement, connected-experience section and footnote 3

text: Samsung states that LYNK Cloud can centrally monitor TV status, update on-screen services, and distribute guest-facing content across supported displays.
limitations: Vendor-stated; LYNK Cloud is sold separately and feature availability varies by region and device.
excerpt: Monitor TV status in real time, update on-screen services and distribute guest-facing content.
locator: Frame hospitality announcement, ‘Managing Hospitality Features From One Platform’

text: Samsung states that LYNK Cloud can expose digital concierge functions, hotel-service booking, and room-service ordering through supported in-room TVs.
limitations: Vendor-stated; availability depends on property integrations and local configuration.
No public evidence in this release quantifies incremental revenue.
excerpt: Guests can access digital concierge features, book hotel services and order room service.
locator: Frame hospitality announcement, LYNK Cloud section

text: Samsung states that LYNK Cloud Business Intelligence can show how guests use supported in-room TV services, including menu-item orders and channel popularity.
limitations: Vendor-stated; analytics availability and lawful data use depend on deployment and governance.
excerpt: Understand how guests use in-room TV services, including frequently ordered menu items or popular TV channels.
locator: Frame hospitality announcement, Business Intelligence paragraph

text: Samsung states that its 2026 Frame hospitality model supports Live Translate subtitles for specified languages and supported broadcast content.
limitations: Vendor-stated; requires supported closed-captioned content and varies by model, region, language, and channel.
Translation is not equivalent to full interface accessibility.
excerpt: Live Translate helps international travelers watch supported content with subtitles in a preferred language.
locator: Frame hospitality announcement, paragraph 76 and footnote 2

text: Samsung states that SmartThings Pro can provide centralized monitoring and control of compatible displays, HVAC, and IoT devices, with APIs for existing systems.
limitations: Vendor-stated; compatible devices, integrations, and features vary by market and deployment.
excerpt: Connect and control compatible hospitality TVs, signage, air conditioning and IoT devices through one dashboard.
locator: AirPlay announcement, SmartThings Pro paragraphs and footnotes

text: Samsung's documented hospitality stack is a vendor-stated example of a hybrid architecture combining displays, cloud management, casting, IoT control, security controls, analytics, and PMS-connected services.
limitations: Reference architecture, not an independent performance comparison or endorsement.
Individual features have separate model, region, integration, and licensing constraints.
excerpt: Display hardware, casting, LYNK Cloud, SmartThings Pro, PMS integration, analytics and security controls appear as one documented stack.
locator: Synthesis across cited Samsung primary sources

text: LG and Apple announced AirPlay availability at more than 60 IHG hotels in North America in April 2024.
limitations: Vendor and partner announcement; property count is deployment availability, not guest outcome evidence.
excerpt: Available at more than 60 IHG hotels in North America.

text: Oracle documentation describes OPERA Cloud guest-engagement, merchandising, mobile-experience, and integration capabilities that can connect PMS records with external hospitality services.
limitations: Vendor-stated platform capability; actual screen integration requires property-specific implementation.
excerpt: OPERA Cloud exposes guest-engagement, merchandising, mobile and integration capabilities.
locator: Product announcement and official user guides

text: Samsung reports supplying more than 6,000 hospitality displays for Star of the Seas and more than 200,000 displays across 28 Royal Caribbean ships over the relationship.
limitations: Vendor-stated case study; counts are not independently audited in this release.
excerpt: More than 6,000 displays on Star of the Seas and more than 200,000 across 28 ships.

text: WCAG 2.2 requires that information and relationships conveyed visually also be programmatically determinable or available in text, and that color not be the only differentiator.
limitations: WCAG conformance for the explorer requires implementation testing beyond citing the standard.
excerpt: Information, structure and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text.

text: NIST identifies hotel property-management systems as attractive attack surfaces and recommends access control, monitoring, tokenization, and zero-trust concepts in its hospitality reference design.
period: historical PMS reference design plus 2024 IoT guidance
limitations: The PMS reference design is older historical context and is not a certification of any cited vendor implementation.
excerpt: Protect sensitive data, enforce role-based access control and monitor for anomalies.
locator: NIST SP 1800-27 abstract and principal recommendations

text: OpenAI's orchestration guidance supports a manager agent retaining responsibility while calling bounded specialist agents as tools.
limitations: Architecture guidance does not itself validate the quality of HXG evidence outputs.
excerpt: A manager can retain control while invoking specialist agents as bounded tools.

text: Microsoft GraphRAG extracts an entity graph and community summaries to support query-focused synthesis across a corpus.
limitations: GraphRAG proposals still require deterministic validation and citation audit before publication.
excerpt: An entity knowledge graph and community summaries support global and local corpus questions.

text: Taken together, independent guest usage data and cross-vendor platform capabilities support treating the in-room display as an experience-orchestration layer rather than only an entertainment device.
limitations: This is a cross-source interpretation, not a measured causal outcome.
Implementation quality, integration, adoption, privacy, and availability determine realized value.
excerpt: Guest usage is substantial while current platforms connect casting, content, services, data and operations.
locator: HXG synthesis across independent and vendor-primary evidence

text: Central device monitoring and error visibility may reduce some on-site support requirements when incidents can be diagnosed or resolved remotely.
limitations: No avoided-dispatch rate or cost is established by the cited sources.
Actual savings require property incident and labor data.
excerpt: Remote monitoring creates a plausible path to fewer on-site interventions; the savings are unmeasured here.

text: A property can model energy savings as baseline energy expenditure multiplied by the controllable share and a verified reduction rate; HXG does not assign a universal savings percentage.
limitations: Requires property baselines, metering, controllable-load estimates, and verified before/after performance.
Vendor capability is not proof of savings.
excerpt: Baseline energy spend × controllable share × verified reduction rate.

text: A property can model screen-enabled ancillary contribution from occupied room nights, screen engagement, offer conversion, and contribution margin; this release provides no universal uplift.
limitations: Requires property-level engagement, conversion, and margin data.
Capability evidence does not establish incremental revenue or causation.
excerpt: Occupied room nights × screen engagement × offer conversion × contribution margin.
